summary: Longitudinal study that holds the model fixed (self-hosted Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Instruct on vLLM) and runs 35 successive Qwen Code CLI releases on 50 stratified SWE-bench Verified tasks, two runs each, to isolate the harness's effect on resolve rate, tokens and tool calls. It adds a mining study of release velocity for five open-source harnesses (Codex, Qwen Code, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, OpenHands) and correlates release-level development and architectural-component changes with quality shifts.

claims.claim: Holding the model fixed, harness releases change agent quality; resolve rate fluctuates (23%-39%) with no significant trend
claims.evidence: Finding 5 / Fig. 6-7: Spearman rho=0.208, p=0.231 vs release order; mean 30.5%. On 50 tasks a 7-point swing is about 3-4 tasks, comparable to binomial noise (SE about 6.5 pp at 30%), so many 'fluctuations' may not be harness effects. Finding 4 treats Wilcoxon p>0.05 between two runs as proof the distributions are 'identical' (absence-of-evidence reasoning); 87.7% per-task agreement still leaves 12.3% flips.

claims.claim: Token consumption grows strongly across releases (about 391K to 668K per task) without effectiveness gains
claims.evidence: Finding 6: rho=0.743, p<0.0001; task-normalized rho=0.751. Robust trend. Case-study magnitudes are inconsistent: §5.4 reports +52% (v0.1.4->v0.1.5) and +131% (v0.2.3->v0.3.0) while §8.2 cites 139% and 182% for the same releases.

claims.claim: Token inflation is driven by ~8% larger initial prompts and 18% more turns
claims.evidence: Finding 8 / Fig. 9: tokens vs turns rho=0.941. Correlational trajectory analysis; the fixed 600 s timeout may interact with turn count and is not discussed as a confound.

claims.claim: Specific development patterns and architectural components (LLM Provider, Context Management, Security, Extensibility) explain quality shifts
claims.evidence: RQ2/RQ3 Tables 7-11: many Spearman correlations around |rho|=0.33-0.55 on n=35 (delta n=34) with Benjamini-Hochberg correction and Cliff's d; observational, single project, many factors tested, so findings are hypotheses rather than causal effects. PR-level case studies are illustrative.

claims.claim: Agent harnesses release 13-28x more often than traditional OSS projects
claims.evidence: RQ0 Findings 1-3 from GitHub mining of five harness repos.

patterns.note: Shows that functional CI passed while token cost rose 52-131% and resolve rate dropped; argues for agent-level regression tracking of resolve rate, tokens and tool calls.
Unbudgeted harness evolution nearly doubled per-task tokens; failed tasks use 2.7x tokens, supporting caps.
Expanding context-management logic associated with worse token efficiency (Finding 15); correlational.
Growth of system prompt and tool schemas compounds per turn (Finding 8).
Uses a 50-task SWE-bench Verified subset as the regression probe.
Single-agent CLI loop studied across versions.

[retag 2026-10-07] Mention only: Agentless is cited as a 'lightweight, non-agentic' point in the design space (§1, §10.1), and the 'State Machine' in the reference architecture (App. A.2) tracks loop execution states, not developer-defined task steps. All 35 Qwen Code releases are the same single-agent ReAct loop, so there is no fixed-workflow comparison.

methodology.sample: 35 releases x 50 SWE-bench Verified tasks (20 easy, 25 medium, 5 hard) x 2 runs = 3,500 executions; RQ0: 5 harness repos
methodology.baselines: Release-to-release comparison; no other harness run under the same model
methodology.models: Single model: Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Instruct via vLLM 0.18.0, harness's default sampling
methodology.variance: Two runs per task; 87.7% binary agreement; Wilcoxon tests between runs; no CIs on per-release resolve rates
methodology.ablations: None directly; component effects inferred by correlation with partial correlations
methodology.contamination_controls: None discussed for SWE-bench Verified memorization by the Qwen model (constant across releases, so affects absolute but not relative numbers)

standards.peer_review: arXiv preprint; ACM TOSEM template header but no acceptance in comment/journal_ref
standards.artifacts: Replication package with all 35 CLI versions, inference/evaluation scripts and raw results (§1, ref Sghaier et al. 2026)

biases.detail: One model; authors note stronger/weaker models may react differently to prompt bloat.
50 tasks per release; resolve-rate differences of a few tasks are within sampling noise.
Controlled analysis on Qwen Code only; title generalizes to 'coding agent quality'.
Token-increase magnitudes for v0.1.5 and v0.3.0 differ between §5.4 (52%, 131%) and §8.2 (139%, 182%).
'Don't blame the LLM' framing, but the study never varies the model, so relative contribution of model vs harness is not measured.
RQ2/RQ3 test many factors on n=35 releases; moderate correlations are presented as component 'risk' guidance.

coi.vendor_products_evaluated: Qwen Code CLI (Alibaba/Qwen) evaluated, largely unfavorably; no author affiliation with Alibaba

coi.detail: Independent academic evaluation of an open-source vendor harness.

verdict_reason: The best-controlled evidence in the batch that the harness, with model held fixed, moves cost substantially and effectiveness noticeably; the token-inflation result is robust. Caveats: one harness, one model, Python-only 50-task probe, resolve-rate swings near noise, correlational component findings, and inconsistent case-study magnitudes.
applicability: Directly informs the team's harness decisions. (1) Pin host/harness versions and treat upgrades of Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, etc. as changes that need a regression check, since functional CI did not catch 52-131% token jumps. (2) Build a small agent-level regression suite from the team's own Java tasks (e.g. 20-50 ingestion and delivery issues across the several repositories with Maven/Gradle tests as the oracle) and track resolve rate, tokens and tool calls per host version; this is host-neutral and fits the 'deterministic CLI decides' rule. (3) Keep shared instructions/specs and tool catalogs small, because prompt growth compounds every turn. Caution: numbers come from Python SWE-bench with one open model and may not transfer in size to Java or frontier models.
